messages:
maya: quick flag — reranker-v2 int8 (ptq) dropped ~0.03 NDCG on webqa-anchor holdout after we switched tokenizer preprocessing. can we triage?
sam: ouch. is that float->int8 only or did we also change doc trimming/prefixing?
maya: only int8 + a tiny change: we started canonicalizing doc html by removing some micro-markup. command I ran: `./run_eval --model reranker-v2-int8 --holdout webqa-anchor --seed 42`
liam: can you paste the eval summary? just the top lines from the harness output pls
maya: paste: 
```
EVAL SUMMARY: model=reranker-v2-int8
NDCG@10: 0.712 (-0.032 vs baseline)
MRR@10: 0.568 (-0.018)
queries=12,842
```
anita: interesting that MRR moved less than NDCG. suggests tail reordering? could be tokenization changing similarity on longer docs.
devon: did we change whitespace/casing normalization in the new canonicalizer? those can move term boundaries.
maya: i only stripped <span data-meta> tags and normalized consecutive whitespace -> single space. no casefold.
sam: can we repro by running float model on the new-canonicalized docs? that would separate quantization vs doc-canon effects.
liam: good call. also try int8 on original corpus (no canonicalization). if float on new corpus still fine then quantization is suspect.
anita: short checklist: 1) float on original; 2) float on canonicalized; 3) int8 on original; 4) int8 on canonicalized. keep eval harness seed fixed.
maya: running 1 & 2 now, will post numbers.
(eval-bot): queued run 1769812346 for job=eval/rerank/1769812346 (approx 18m ETA)
maya: results for float: original corpus -> NDCG@10 0.744 (baseline). float: canonicalized -> NDCG@10 0.741 (-0.003).
liam: ok canonicalization cost is tiny. that points back to quantization.
sam: do we use per-channel quantization or symmetric? and what calibration set?
maya: PTQ symmetric int8 with KL calibration on 5k samples from train split. same as before.
devon: can we test with per-tensor vs per-channel? sometimes attention kernels are sensitive to scale mismatch.
anita: also check tokenization-induced length changes: canonicalization reduced average doc tokens by ~6% (weird). int8 might be brittle to that distribution shift if activation ranges were calibrated on longer sequences.
liam: run: `./inspect_token_stats --corpus original canonicalized --model tok-vocab --out tok-stats.csv`
maya: ran tok stats: avg tokens original 384 -> canonicalized 360. token length delta concentrated in boilerplate docs.
sam: experiment plan: A) PTQ calibrate on canonicalized corpus; B) PTQ per-channel; C) small L2 fold update (recalibrate bias) if possible.
devon: also try hybrid quant (int8 weights + float activations) to see if activation quant kills tail.
maya: will queue A/B/C and post numbers here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
(eval-bot): enqueued jobs [1769812350,1769812351,1769812352].
